excerpt: Savannah's most crash-prone intersections and roads, what makes each dangerous, and your options if you are injured on one.
keyTakeaways: Savannah's most dangerous intersections — including Abercorn and White Bluff, I-16 at Chatham Parkway, and DeRenne at Truman Parkway — produce hundreds of crashes annually. Georgia's two-year statute of limitations (O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33) and modified comparative fault rule (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33) govern how victims can recover compensation for injuries caused by red-light running, distracted driving, and poor road design across Chatham County.

faqs.question: What is the most dangerous intersection in Savannah, Georgia?
faqs.answer: The intersection of Abercorn Street and White Bluff Road is consistently ranked as Savannah's most dangerous intersection, producing the highest number of crashes and injury-related hospital transports in Chatham County. Other high-risk intersections include I-16 at Chatham Parkway, King George Boulevard at Abercorn Street, and DeRenne Avenue at Truman Parkway.

faqs.question: What should I do immediately after a car accident at a Savannah intersection?
faqs.answer: Call 911 to report the crash, seek immediate medical attention even if you feel fine, document the scene with photographs, exchange information with all involved drivers and witnesses, and contact a Savannah car accident lawyer before giving any recorded statements to insurance companies. Under Georgia law, the police report and your medical records become critical evidence in your injury claim.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a car accident lawsuit in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33, you have two years from the date of your accident to file a personal injury lawsuit in Georgia. Missing this statute of limitations deadline typically means losing your right to compensation. South Carolina allows three years under S.C. Code § 15-3-530.

faqs.question: Can I recover compensation if I was partially at fault for an intersection crash in Georgia?
faqs.answer: Yes. Georgia follows a modified comparative fault rule under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, which allows you to recover compensation as long as you are less than 50% at fault for the accident. However, your total award is reduced by your percentage of fault. For example, if you are 20% at fault and your damages total $100,000, your recovery would be $80,000.

faqs.question: Why is Abercorn Street so dangerous in Savannah?
faqs.answer: Abercorn Street is Savannah's most dangerous road corridor because it carries enormous traffic volumes through heavily commercialized areas with constant turning movements, driveway conflicts, and inadequate traffic infrastructure. Multiple intersections along Abercorn — including White Bluff Road, King George Boulevard, Rio Road, and Victory Drive — rank among the city's most crash-prone locations.

faqs.question: Can I sue the city if a dangerous road design caused my Savannah accident?
faqs.answer: Potentially, yes. If a government entity's failure to properly design, maintain, or signal an intersection contributed to your crash, you may have a claim against the City of Savannah, Chatham County, or the Georgia Department of Transportation. These claims have strict notice requirements and shortened filing deadlines, so consulting an attorney promptly is essential.
